 Jodhpur, (Raj.)

(In Judicial Custody At Central Jail,
 Jodhpur)
 ----Petitioners  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through PP  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. J.S. Choudhary, Sr. Adv. assisted  by Mr. Pradeep Choudhary For Respondent(s) : Mr. Shrawan Singh, PP
Mr. Hari Shanker Shrimali for  complainant
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJENDRA PRAKASH SONI Order 09/10/2024 1.

Arrested in furtherance of FIR No.84/2022, registered at Police Station Mandore, District Jodhpur City East, petitioners have filed this application under Section 483 BNSS (Section 439 of old code) for releasing them on bail.

The petitioners are charged for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 472, 474, 120-B of the I.P.C.
2.

Heard arguments advanced by learned counsel for the petitioners, learned public prosecutor and carefully perused the entire material available on record.
Bhawana vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:41451) on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150523864/
1 [2024:RJ-JD:41451] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-11786/2024]
3.
Learned Public Prosecutor for the State as well as learned counsel for the complainant have strongly objected the different submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioners.

They thus,
crave rejection of the petitioners' bail application.
4. I have given my anxious consideration to the rival submissions with reference to material placed before me.
Factual report produced by the learned Public Prosecutor is taken on record.
5. On perusal of the record and upon consideration of the submissions, it would be clear that the dispute between parties is purely civil in nature.
The alleged agreement to sale was executed in the year 2011 and effect thereto has been given on 23.01.2020.

Admittedly prior to lodging of the FIR,
complainant did not opt for any civil litigation for cancellation of sale deed in dispute.
Both the parties are close relatives.

6. Having considered the material available on record; the arguments advanced by counsel for the petitioners particularly the facts narrated above and the fact that bail rejection order goes to show that petitioners are not involved in any other case; that trial is likely to take its own considerable time and taking note of all these aspects I do not intend to go into the merits of the matter but of the considered view that the petitioners have available to them substantial grounds so as to question the prosecution case and no useful purpose would be served by keeping the petitioners in detention for an indefinite period therefore, I am inclined to grant indulgence of bail to the petitioners at this stage.
7.
Consequently, the present bail application is allowed and it is directed that the accused-petitioners 1. Bhawana W/o Shri [2024:RJ-JD:41451] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-11786/2024]

Rajendra Kumar and 2. Rajendra S/o Shri Devi Lal, arrested in connection with the FIR No.84/2022, registered at Police Station Mandore, District Jodhpur City East shall be released on bail provided each of them furnish a personal bond and two surety bonds of sufficient amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial court with the stipulation to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.

This order is subject to the condition that accused,
within 7 days of their release, and sureties on the day of furnishing bail, will also furnish details of their all bank accounts, with bank and branch name, in shape of an affidavit, and submit legible copy of their Aadhar cards as well as copy of front page of Bank pass book, for smooth recovery of penalty amount, if there arise a need for recovery of penalty under Section 446 Cr.P.C in future.
(RAJENDRA PRAKASH SONI),J 410-suraj/-
